### Sheet: Population Rules

POPULATION RULES - HOW TO FILL EACH FIELD FROM PAYROLL  

| Row | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | **═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES ═══** |  |  |  |
| 4 | Casilla 77 - base employment income | Payroll engine (tax) | Accumulate, across every RESIDENT employee paid in the month, the taxable base actually used to compute the withholding: the ET art. 388 DEPURATED base - gross taxable payments less non-constitutive income (mandatory health, pension and solidarity-fund contributions), less the art. 387 deductions elected in writing by the employee, less the 25% exempt income of art. 206 num. 10, subject to the 40% and 1,340-UVT caps. Do NOT report the gross. Non-resident foreign natural persons are not accumulated here: they are reported as sheet-2 rows in the 'Pagos al exterior' section at the nominal (gross) value. Pension income the employer pays itself is not accumulated here: it goes to casilla 78. Round the accumulated total to the nearest 1,000 (ET art. 577), once, at the end - never round each employee and then sum. | The casilla also sweeps in fees, services and commissions paid to NATURAL persons that are withheld under the art. 383 table (ET art. 383 para. 2, added by Law 2277 of 2022 art. 8). Payroll supplies only the EMPLOYMENT component; the fee, service and commission component is supplied by the employer's accounts-payable or tax function, which also owns casillas 79 / 95. |
| 5 | Casilla 93 - withholding employment income | Payroll engine (tax) | Accumulate the withholding at source actually withheld on work income from resident natural persons in the month: wage type 2552 'Income Tax (employee)', plus the withholding deducted on 21129 (terminations) and, where the WTC classifies them as withholding actually deducted, on 25832 (stock-award vesting) and 25833 (IC local), in the month it is practised, across every pay group and run. Exclude the contingent withholding of ET arts. 126-1 / 126-4 - the withholding computed without the AFC and voluntary-pension contributions less the withholding computed with them - which is practised by the fund on an early withdrawal and never by the employer, and exclude the theoretical and hypothetical wage types 21114, 21619 and 25834, which carry no withholding actually practised (wage type 21330 is included only where it carries the withholding actually deducted). Withholding on the pensions the employer pays itself (21140, 21155) goes to casilla 94, not here. An employee's monthly withholding is not rounded: accumulate the unrounded figures. The approximation to the nearest 1,000 applies only to the Form 350 return values (DUR 1625 de 2016 art. 1.6.1.11.11), that is, to the casilla 93 total. Reconcile casilla 93 plus casilla 94 to the sum of RetencionFuente (NIE177) across every electronic payroll document for the same month BEFORE filing. Select the runs by their payment date - payment or credit to account, whichever comes first - not by the pay period they settle (ET art. 383; ET art. 27; instruction guide of Res. DIAN 000031/2024). | An employee whose depurated base falls in the 0% band contributes zero here but still contributes their base to casilla 77. Excluding the base is a common and material error. |
| 6 | Casillas 78 / 94 - pension income | Payroll engine (tax) | Populate where the EMPLOYER itself pays pensions (the retirees' pay group). Casilla 78: the monthly amount EXCEEDING 1,000 UVT (COP 52,374,000 in 2026) under ET art. 206 num. 5, for the wage types classified as pension income; the pension-income classification of each wage type (casilla 78 rather than casilla 77) comes from the Wage Type Catalogue (WTC) attribute. Casilla 94: the withholding actually practised on that excess - wage type 21140 'Personal Income Tax Withholding-Retirees- 6799' and wage type 21155 'Income Tax Pensioner'. Neither amount enters casillas 77 / 93. Where the pension is paid by a pension fund, the fund is the withholding agent and nothing is reported here. | Colombia has no employer year-end reconciliation, so an error here is amended only by a corrective return, not by a December true-up. |
| 7 | Casilla 12 - regional tax office | Company master data | Copy the code from casilla 12 of the entity's RUT. It is a static configuration attribute; it does not change with the period and must not be re-derived monthly. | A branch structure does not change this casilla - the return is filed for the principal domicile of the legal entity. |
| 8 | **═══ CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES ═══** |  |  |  |
| 9 | Nil period | Engine (control) | Where NO operation subject to withholding occurred in the month, DO NOT file. ET art. 606 para. 2 makes the return non-obligatory for such a period. This is unusual: the electronic payroll and PILA have no equivalent exemption, so a month with employees but no withholding still produces those two filings while producing no Form 350. | Filing an all-zero return is not an error, but it creates a record that must then be amended if a late payment is discovered. Prefer not filing where the exemption genuinely applies, and document the decision. |
| 10 | Payment must accompany the return | Engine (control) | Casilla 980 (payment total) must equal casilla 138 (total withholdings mas sanciones). ET art. 580-1: a withholding return filed WITHOUT full payment produces NO legal effect, and no administrative act is needed to say so. Until the taxpayer files again WITH payment, the original filing is treated as never made. | This is the single most expensive procedural trap on this return: a filed-but-unpaid return accrues late-filing penalties as though nothing had been filed. |
| 11 | Do not key the portal-derived casillas | Engine (control) | The DIAN service derives casillas 55, 56, 57, 58, 109, 110, 111 and 112 (from the sheet-2 annex totals 148 to 155), 130, 134, 136, 138 and 147 (145 x 146). Supply only the inputs. Attempting to key a derived casilla either fails or, worse, creates an inconsistency the portal silently overwrites. | For the non-resident block this means payroll supplies sheet-2 ROWS - casillas 141 to 146 - and never the sheet-1 casillas 109 to 112. |
| 12 | Counterparty-type separation | Engine (accumulation) | The 2024 form separates withholding on NATURAL persons from withholding on LEGAL persons across the whole grid. The engine must therefore accumulate withholding by counterparty type from the transaction level, not classify it at reporting time. The pre-2024 form did not require this and a migrated accumulation will not carry the flag. | Payroll is inherently natural-person only, so its own accumulation is unambiguous. The risk lies in a shared withholding ledger where supplier and employee withholding are commingled. |
| 13 | **═══ AMOUNT FORMAT RULES ═══** |  |  |  |
| 14 | All money casillas | Engine (formatting) | Whole pesos, then rounded to the NEAREST 1,000 under ET art. 577. Apply the rounding ONCE, to the accumulated casilla value, not to each contributing record. No decimals, no thousand separators in the transmitted value. | Rounding each employee to the nearest 1,000 and then summing produces a total that can differ from the correctly rounded aggregate by several thousand pesos across a large population. |
| 15 | Three conventions must not be blended | Engine (formatting) | The SAME withholding appears as three different numbers across the Colombian artefacts: nearest-1,000 here; two decimals round-half-to-even in the electronic payroll; and irrelevant in PILA, which carries contributions not tax. Store the unrounded figure once and apply each convention at output. | The reconciliation between casilla 93 plus casilla 94 and SUM(NIE177) must therefore be performed on the UNROUNDED values with a tolerance, not on the rounded ones. |
| 16 | Minimum penalty | Engine (control) | Where casilla 137 is populated, the amount cannot be below 10 UVT. For 2026 that is 10 x 52,374 = COP 523,740. For a CORRECTIVE return the minimum is 10 UVT of the year in which the ORIGINAL return was filed, not of the current year. | A correction of a 2024 return filed in 2026 uses the 2024 UVT for the minimum penalty. Store the original filing year with the correction. |
| 17 | **═══ PAYROLL-SPECIFIC POPULATION RULES ═══** |  |  |  |
| 18 | Non-resident employees - sheet 2 rows | Payroll engine (tax) | For each non-resident foreign natural person, create one sheet-2 row per country and treaty status in the 'Pagos al exterior' section. Set casilla 141 to SIN CONVENIO or CON CONVENIO; casilla 142 to concept 5 (Prestaciones de servicios y compensacion por servicios personales) for non-treaty countries or concept 24 (Rentas de trabajo) for treaty countries; casilla 143 to Persona natural; casilla 144 to the DIAN country-table code of the country of tax residence (the same code used in the RUT and in exogenous information); casilla 145 to the NOMINAL (gross) payment - not a depurated base, because ET art. 408 admits no depuration; and casilla 146 to 20.00, or to the treaty rate. The employee is excluded from casillas 77 and 93. The portal computes casilla 147 and the four totals. | Rows for the same country, concept and person type may be aggregated. Do NOT aggregate across treaty statuses or across concepts - the rate and the treaty article differ. Directors' fees belong in concept 25 and employer-paid pensions in concept 27, never in 24. |
| 19 | Residence switch mid-year | Payroll engine (tax) | Carry a residence flag with an effective date on the employee record and re-evaluate it every period against ET art. 10 - presence exceeding 183 calendar days, continuous or not, in any 365-day period. Until the test is met, report the employee on sheet 2 at the flat 20%. From the payment FOLLOWING the date the test is met, report on sheet 1 casillas 77 and 93 under the art. 383 table. Never restate the earlier months. | DIAN Concept 011108 of 29 June 2026 expressly rejects withholding under art. 383 from day one in anticipation of future residence, even on a contract exceeding 183 days. Withholding is determined at the moment of each payment on the status then held. There is no payroll true-up; the employee reconciles on their own return. |
| 20 | Work performed entirely abroad | Payroll engine (tax) | Where a NON-RESIDENT performs the work entirely outside Colombia, the income is foreign-source and there is NO Colombian withholding and nothing to report on this return - neither sheet 1 nor sheet 2. Where a RESIDENT performs work abroad, the income IS taxable on the worldwide basis and goes to casillas 77 and 93 as normal. | The distinguishing attribute is the place-of-work country carried on the electronic payroll (NIE050). Keep the two records consistent: a document showing LugarTrabajoPais other than CO for a non-resident should produce no Form 350 line. |
| 21 | Casilla 129 - reversing an over-withholding | Payroll engine | Where an employee's withholding is adjusted downward in a later month - a retroactive change to the art. 387 deductions, a cancelled payment, or an arithmetic error - report the reversal in casilla 129 of the month in which the correction is made, rather than correcting the earlier return. Where the month's withholding is insufficient to absorb the credit, the instruction guide permits carrying it to the immediately following periods. | Casilla 129 also carries reintegros of non-transferable withholding attributable to a resident natural-person beneficiary or a resident foreign investor under DUR 1625 de 2016 art. 1.2.4.37 - not a payroll case, but the same casilla. |
| 22 | Casilla 27 and the art. 114-1 exoneration | Company configuration | Populate casilla 27 only where the employer is a LEGAL person exonerated from employer contributions under ET art. 114-1. The SAME exoneration test - employees earning less than 10 SMMLV (COP 17,509,050 in 2026; salary-constituting payments of the month AND health IBC both below 10 SMMLV - see CO-PILA-003 T2R2-076) - drives PILA file tipo 1 field 33 and PILA Record Tipo 2 field 76. Configure the test ONCE and consume it in both places. | The exoneration is tested MONTHLY and PER EMPLOYEE for PILA purposes, but the self-withholding activity code here is an entity-level, static attribute. Do not conflate the two granularities. |
| 23 | **═══ CROSS-FIELD VALIDATIONS ═══** |  |  |  |
| 24 | Casilla 25 and casilla 26 | Engine (validation) | Both blank on an initial return; both populated on a corrective one. Casilla 26 must carry the casilla-4 form number of the return being amended. | A corrective return with casilla 26 blank is treated as a new initial return and produces a duplicate filing for the period. |
| 25 | Casillas 7-10 versus casilla 11 | Engine (validation) | A LEGAL person populates casilla 11 and leaves 7 to 10 blank; a NATURAL person does the reverse. The DIAN service auto-fills whichever applies from the RUT. | Both blocks populated is a RUT inconsistency, not a form error - resolve it in the RUT. |
| 26 | Casilla 27 and casilla 28 | Engine (validation) | From the June 2026 period casilla 28 is disabled and requires no entry (DIAN Oficio 15662 of 2026; provisional suspension of arts. 2 to 8 of Decree 572 of 2025 by the Consejo de Estado on 7 May 2026). Leave casilla 28 blank and populate casilla 27 as described in its own row. | Do not key a rate in 28: it is disabled from the June 2026 period. |
| 27 | Casillas 982, 983 and 994 | Engine (validation) | Where casilla 982 is populated, casilla 983 (professional card number) is mandatory and casilla 994 (with qualifications) becomes available. Where 982 is blank, 983 and 994 must be blank. | An unsigned return that required an accountant's or auditor's signature is defective. |
| 28 | Casilla 138 and casilla 980 | Engine (validation) | They must be equal. Block submission where they are not. | ET art. 580-1 makes an underpaid return legally ineffective. This is a hard stop, not a warning. |
| 29 | Cross-report reconciliation | Engine (reconciliation) | Before filing, assert: SUM(NIE177) over all electronic payroll documents for the month, unrounded, equals the unrounded accumulation behind casilla 93 plus casilla 94, within a tolerance of one peso per employee. Assert also that the employee count behind casilla 77 equals the number of validated electronic payroll documents for the month. | A mismatch almost always means either an employee was paid without a electronic payroll document, or a document was rejected and not re-transmitted. Both are deductibility failures, not just reporting failures. |

### Sheet: Sample File

SAMPLE FILE - CHANNEL STATEMENT AND COMPLETED-FORM RENDERING  
WHY THERE IS NO SAMPLE FILE  
════════════  
Form 350 is submitted as an ONLINE PORTAL FORM through the DIAN Services  
Informaticos Electronicos (Muisca) at www.dian.gov.co, signed with the  
Instrumento de Firma Electronica (IFE).  
DIAN publishes NO XSD, NO cahier des charges and NO import template for this  
form. Res. DIAN 000227 de 2025 art. 1.2.2.26 par. 1 states only that filers must  
use "los Servicios Informaticos dispuestos por la entidad, utilizando el  
Electronic Signature Instrument (IFE)", and that DIAN "pondra a disposicion el  
Formulario numero 350 en forma virtual en la pagina web www.dian.gov.co para su  
diligenciamiento y presentacion".  
Fabricating an XML or CSV sample for this filing would therefore be inventing a  
format that does not exist. What follows instead is a COMPLETED-FORM RENDERING -  
the casilla-value set the engine must deliver to the portal operator or to the  
robotic-process step that keys it. This is the actual deliverable.  
Casillas marked [PORTAL] are computed by the DIAN service and must NOT be keyed.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------  
CONTRAST THAT MATTERS  
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------  
Same employee, same COP 12,000,000 salary, same month:  
RESIDENT base 8.190.000 (depurated, ET art. 388) withholding 617.000  
NON-RESIDENT base 12.000.000 (GROSS, ET art. 408) withholding 2.400.000  
The non-resident withholding is 3.9 times the resident figure, and it is reported  
on a DIFFERENT SHEET of the same return. An employee who acquires residence  
mid-year moves from sheet 2 to sheet 1 PROSPECTIVELY, from the payment following  
the date the 183-day test is met. The earlier months are never restated  
(DIAN Concepto 011108 of 29 June 2026).  
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------  
PORTAL SCREEN-LEVEL BEHAVIOUR  
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------  
The casilla numbers, labels and arithmetic above follow the official form design  
and instruction guide. The portal's screen-level behaviour - field ordering,  
mandatory-field prompts and any bulk-entry facility DIAN offers to large filers -  
is not published by DIAN. The engine's deliverable is the reconciled casilla-value set  
(Report Matrix); the keying or robotic-process path is a portal-integration configuration, not a file format.

| 13 | Frequency | Monthly. Required while the employment relationship subsists, even with no payment in the month |
| 14 | Submission Deadline | 2nd-16th BUSINESS DAY of the month following the period, by the LAST TWO DIGITS of the employer ID (Decree 780 of 2016 art. 3.2.2.1) |

| 16 | File Extension | Not prescribed by the annex. The file extension is held in the information-operator configuration, as published by the chosen operador. |
| 17 | Character Encoding | Not prescribed by the annex. The character encoding is held in the information-operator configuration, as published by the chosen operador. |
| 18 | Record Types / Sections | Record Tipo 1 (Encabezado); Record Tipo 2 (Liquidacion) |
| 19 | Version | v1.2 |
| 22 | DETAILED COMPLIANCE NOTES (Colombia-specific) |  |
| 23 | SUBMISSION CHANNEL |  |
| 24 | - Channel: file_upload (fixed-width) into a PORTAL operated by a licensed private information operator \| Portal: the chosen operador's web site (the operador is licensed by the Ministry of Health and Social Protection; the employer selects one commercially) \| Source: Res. MSPS 2388 de 2016 Technical Annex 2 s.0 and s.2.1.1.2.1, and Decree 780 of 2016 art. 3.2.3.9 as substituted by Decree 1990 of 2016 |  |
| 25 | - THE SOCIAL-SECURITY CHANNEL IS NOT THE TAX CHANNEL. PILA never touches DIAN Muisca, and Form 350 never touches an information operator. Labelling either with the other's portal is a category error. |  |
| 26 | - Two modalities exist: 1 Electronica (the employer keys or uploads on the operador's site) and 2 Asistida (the operador's call centre keys it). Where Decree 780 of 2016 art. 3.2.3.9 para. 2 exceptionally permits assisted payment, the modality field must still say ELECTRONICA and the operador reports those employers to the Ministry through SISPRO structure PUB019EXPE by the fifth business day of the following month. |  |
| 27 | - The layout is byte-exact and published, so this Spec CAN and DOES carry a real fixed-width sample on Sheet 9 - generated programmatically from the position table so that the record lengths are exactly 567, 359 and 693 characters. |  |
| 28 | - Operator upload envelope: each operador wraps the two files in its own upload envelope and may add validations. The wrapper and any operador-specific validations are published by the chosen operador and held in the information-operator configuration; the two files inside the envelope follow the annex layout byte for byte. |  |
| 29 | INTEGRATION TYPE AND DIRECTION |  |
| 30 | - Integration: outbound file generation and inbound response handling. Outbound: the two fixed-width files. Inbound: the operador's settlement response. |  |
| 31 | - The inbound leg (CO-IN-PILA-SETTLEMENT) is specified here rather than in a separate workbook because it is the response half of one exchange and is keyed on this filing's own return number (T2R1-017). The engine must reconcile the settled contributions against its own computation, capture the return number and payment date, and detect rejected contributor records. Each operador's response layout is proprietary and is published by the operador itself - it has no published national standard, so this workbook carries no field-level specification for it; the chosen operador's layout is held in the information-operator configuration. |  |
| 32 | - product_mapping_required = true. PILA needs FIVE contribution bases per employee (pension, health, occupational risk, CCF, and the separate uncapped parafiscal base), FOUR day counts, and sixteen change-event flags with their date pairs. None of these can be derived at reporting time from a single gross figure. |  |
| 33 | - Owned upstream: the information operator's own file wrapper and portal. Mercans produces the two annex-conformant files; the operador owns everything after that. |  |
| 34 | RESIDENT / NON-RESIDENT TREATMENT |  |
| 35 | - PILA IS NOT A TAX FILING and carries NO residence concept. A non-resident employee working in Colombia under a Colombian contract contributes to social security on exactly the same terms as a resident - same bases, same rates, same ceiling and floor. The flat 20% of ET art. 408 has no application here. |  |
| 36 | - The one immigration-related field is 'Foreign national not liable to contribute to pensions' (T2R2-007), and it is about PENSION AFFILIATION, not tax residence. AT2 v30 (24-07-2026) §2.1.2.3.3 (campo 7) defines it as a foreign citizen who is not obliged by law to contribute to the General Pension System but must contribute to the other subsystems. The legal text behind the configuration is Ley 100 de 1993 art. 15 num. 2 (as modified by Ley 797 de 2003 art. 3): foreigners who remain in the country under an employment contract and are not covered by a pension regime of their country of origin or of any other country are voluntary affiliates. The specification states no rule beyond that text; the flag is an option per employee, kept with this citation. Health, occupational risk and the parafiscal levies remain fully payable. |  |
| 37 | - It follows that the same employee can be simultaneously (a) withheld at 20% on sheet 2 of Form 350 as a non-resident, and (b) reported in PILA on ordinary terms. Do not let the tax residence flag leak into the PILA population rules. |  |
| 38 | - The mirror case - 'Colombian abroad' (T2R2-008) - is also not a tax field. It suppresses the DIVIPOLA work-location fields and enables the foreign filing date in T2R2-097. |  |
| 39 | RELATED FILINGS / CROSS-REFERENCES |  |
| 40 | - The employee health, pension and solidarity-fund figures must reconcile to electronic payroll NIE163, NIE166 and NIE168 / NIE170 (CO-DIAN-001), allowing for the different rounding conventions - PILA rounds UP to the next 100, the XML uses two decimals round-half-to-even. |  |
| 41 | - The ET art. 114-1 exoneration in A1-033 and T2R2-076 rests on the SAME test as Form 350 casilla 27 (CO-DIAN-002). Configure it once. |  |
| 42 | - The employee's mandatory health and pension contributions - the amounts settled here - are the non-taxable income de renta that reduce the Form 350 casilla 77 base and are reported annually at Form 220 casillas 53-54 (CO-DIAN-004) and Format 2276 numerals 23-24 (CO-DIAN-005). |  |
| 43 | - PILA return types T and F (Sistema General de Participaciones) and types I and Y (independent workers) are out of scope - public sector and non-employees respectively. This specification covers the private-sector employer return. |  |
| 44 | - The occupational-risk premium (T2R2-063) and the employer's share of pension, health and the levies never appear on the electronic payroll, because that document reports only what the employee accrued and what was deducted from the employee. |  |


### Sheet: Payroll Scope Summary

PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY - INTEGRATED CONTRIBUTION SETTLEMENT RETURN (PILA) - SOCIAL SECURITY AND PAYROLL LEVIES  
PURPOSE: Tell the developer WHO is reported on the monthly PILA settlement and what happens to a borderline case.  

| Row | SCENARIO | REPORT? | NOTES / REASONING |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | **═══ WHO GETS REPORTED ═══** |  |  |
| 6 | Indefinite-term employee (indefinite-term contract) | YES | The core private-sector population. CST art. 47; Ley 2466 de 2025 art. 5. |
| 7 | Fixed-term employee (fixed-term contract, max 4 years) | YES | Identical reporting treatment to an indefinite-term contract. CST art. 46; Ley 2466 de 2025 art. 6. |
| 8 | Specific-work or task employee (contract por obra o labor) | YES | An employment contract; CST art. 46. Electronic payroll TipoContrato = 3 (Obra o Labor). |
| 9 | Occasional / accidental / transitory worker (< 1 month, non-core activity) | YES | Still an employee under CST art. 6. Reported on every filing; the PILA return type and the day counts differ, not the obligation. |
| 10 | Part-time employee | YES | Colombia has no separate part-time regime. Reported normally; the PILA contribution base is floored at 1 SMMLV (COP 1,750,905) except for the worker type 51 partial-time regime. |
| 11 | All-inclusive salary employee (all-inclusive salary, >= 13 SMMLV) | YES | CST art. 132 num. 2. Reported with the integral-salary flag set; the contribution base is 70% of the integral salary, and the electronic payroll carries SalarioIntegral = true. |
| 12 | Apprentice (apprenticeship contract) | YES | Law 2466 of 2025 art. 21 converted the apprenticeship into a special fixed-term LABOUR contract, regulated by Decree 0223 of 5 March 2026. Electronic payroll TipoContrato = 4; PILA tipo cotizante 19 'Aprendices etapa lectiva Ley 2466 de 2025' for the lectiva phase from the health period of August 2025 (code 12 only for earlier periods). For health periods before August 2025, code 19 covers the productive phase; from the health period of August 2025, AT2 v30 names no code for the productive phase (AT2 v30 §2.1.2.3.1 campo 5, types 12 and 19). |
| 13 | Intern / practical placement (practicas o pasantias) | YES | Electronic payroll TipoContrato = 5. Reported where remunerated. |
| 14 | Teleworkers and remote workers | YES | Law 1221 of 2008 as amended by Law 2466 of 2025 arts. 52-54. No reporting difference; the electronic payroll carries a dedicated Teletrabajo earning element (NIE158). |
| 15 | Resident foreign national under a Colombian contract | YES | Full reporting. Withheld under the ET art. 383 progressive table once tax residence is acquired. |
| 16 | NON-RESIDENT foreign national under a Colombian contract | YES | IN SCOPE and frequently mis-configured. Withheld at the flat 20% of ET art. 408 on the GROSS, with no art. 388 depuration, until the 183-day residence test is met (DIAN Concept 011108 of 29 June 2026). See the resident / non-resident block in the Report Matrix. |
| 17 | Employed old-age pensioner in active service | YES | PILA worker sub-type 01; no pension contribution (PILA pension rate field = 0), health and the levies still apply. |
| 18 | Executive director / statutory legal representative holding an employment contract | YES | Reported as an ordinary employee where an employment contract exists. |
| 19 | Independent contractor (service contract) | NO | Not an employee. The contractor self-files PILA on 40% of fees (return types I / Y, descoped) and is reported by the payer in the third-party information return, not in this employer filing. Withholding on their fees does pass through Form 350, but under a different casilla. |
| 20 | Public-sector employee (contributor type 47, SGP-funded entity) | NO | Public-sector only; PILA return types T and F (Sistema General de Participaciones) are out of scope - this specification covers the private-sector employer return. |
| 21 | Non-executive director paid fees only (junta directiva) | NO | Not an employee: a director paid fees only holds no employment contract (an executive director who holds one is reported under the row 'Executive director / statutory legal representative holding an employment contract'), so there is no dependent-worker record to report in this employer filing. The fee recipient contributes as an independent on their own return (types I / Y, out of scope), the same treatment as the independent contractor. |
| 22 | Pensioner whose pension is paid by a fund, not by the employer | NO | The paying fund is the withholding agent and the reporting party, not the employer. A pensioner whose pension the employer pays directly is not reported in this return for that pension: the employer, as pension payer type 01 Empleador, reports the pensioner on the pensioners' PILA under Anexo Tecnico 3 'Aportes a Seguridad Social de Pensionados' (CO-PILA-007; Res. MSPS 2388 de 2016 art. 1, Anexo Tecnico 3; AT3 v15 §1.2.4, p. 13). If that pensioner also works for the employer, the employment is reported in this return (row 'Employed old-age pensioner in active service'). |
| 23 | **═══ AMOUNTS AND CONCEPTS REPORTED ═══** |  |  |
| 24 | Salary and salary-constituting payments | YES | The core of all five contribution bases (CST art. 127). |
| 25 | Pacted non-salary payments within the 40% clamp | NO | Payments agreed as non-salary under an express CST art. 128 pact are excluded from the contribution base - but only up to 40% of total remuneration. Ley 1393 de 2010 art. 30 adds the EXCESS over 40% back into the base, and that added-back amount must be separately identifiable because it is in the contribution base but out of the statutory-benefit base. |
| 26 | Statutory transport allowance | NO | Not salary for contribution purposes. It IS in the base of cesantias, interest on cesantias and prima (Ley 1 de 1963 art. 7), not of the CST art. 64 dismissal indemnity - a different base, and one of the sharpest traps in Colombian payroll. |
| 27 | Paid rest days | YES | In the CCF base (campo 45, T2R2-045) and in the PARAFISCAL base (campo 95, T2R2-095): Ley 21 de 1982 art. 17 defines one monthly salary payroll for the Subsidio Familiar (CCF), SENA, ESAP and Escuelas Industriales e Institutos Técnicos, which includes the payments 'verificados por descansos remunerados de ley y convencionales o contractuales'. Paid rest days include vacation enjoyed and vacation paid in cash, during employment or on termination (Consejo de Estado, Sala de Consulta, concept 2027 of 2010-10-04). The ICBF base is the same payroll (Ley 89 de 1988 art. 1 par. 1). |
| 28 | Contribution base ceiling of 25 SMMLV | YES | COP 43,772,625 in 2026. Applies to pension, health and occupational risk only. Does NOT apply to the CCF base in campo 45 (monthly salary payroll, Ley 21 de 1982 art. 17; 70% for an integral salary, Ley 789 de 2002 art. 49) nor to the parafiscal base in campo 95 - both are uncapped. |
| 29 | Contribution base floor of 1 SMMLV | YES | COP 1,750,905 in 2026, except for the partial-time regime (contributor type 51), which uses hours worked in campo 96. |
| 30 | All-inclusive salary at 70% of the integral salary | YES | CST art. 132 num. 2. Flagged in campo 41 and applied to all four IBC fields. |
| 31 | Employer contributions | YES | PILA is the ONLY artefact that reports the employer's cost - pension 12%, health 8.5%, occupational risk 0.348% to 8.7%, CCF 4%, SENA 2%, ICBF 3%. |
| 32 | Employee deductions | YES | Pension 4%, health 4%, solidarity fund 1% to 2%. Reported as part of the total contribution, not as a separate deduction line. |
| 33 | Income tax withholding | NO | PILA is a contribution settlement, not a tax return. Withholding goes on Form 350. |
| 34 | SENA and ICBF for employees under 10 SMMLV where the employer is exonerated | NO | Where the employer flag A1-033 is S and the employee's monthly flag T2R2-076 is S - salary-constituting payments of the month and health IBC both below 10 SMMLV (COP 17,509,050 in 2026) - the SENA 2% and ICBF 3% rates and values (T2R2-066 to T2R2-069) are reported as zero, together with the employer health 8.5% (ET art. 114-1; DIAN Concepto 008380 de 2024 and 007196 de 2025; AT2 v30 campo 76). Nothing else is exonerated: pension, occupational risk and the CCF 4% in the row below remain payable in full. |
| 35 | CCF 4% for the same employees | YES | The family compensation fund is NEVER exonerated under art. 114-1. The only relief is the Ley 1429 de 2010 art. 5 regime, flagged separately in A1-034. |
| 36 | **═══ TIMING AND RELATIONSHIP ═══** |  |  |
| 37 | Reported on the accrual (causacion) date | NO | Every Colombian payroll filing is keyed to the PAYMENT or credit-in-account date, not to the accrual date. A December salary paid in January falls in the January filing. |
| 38 | Reported on the payment or credit-in-account date | YES | The universal Colombian rule - payment or credit in account. Applies to the electronic payroll (DIAN Resolution 000227 of 2025 art. 1.5.3.2.2), to Form 350, to Form 220 and to Format 2276. |
| 39 | A semi-monthly payroll produces two filings a month | NO | It does not. The electronic payroll is expressly ONE monthly document per employee 'irrespective of whether the obliged party makes payments in different or shorter periods' (Res. DIAN 000227 de 2025 art. 1.5.3.2.2). PILA and Form 350 are likewise monthly. |
| 40 | Nil period still filed | YES | The return is required for every month in which the employment relationship subsists, even with no payment in the month (Report Matrix, Frequency; filing calendar in Decree 780 of 2016 art. 3.2.2.1). An employee with no pay in the month is reported with the change event that explains it - SLN with its date pair and reduced day counts, as in the row 'Employee on unpaid leave for the whole month'. |
| 41 | Corrections handled by re-filing the whole period | VARIES | Electronic payroll: NO - a dedicated adjustment note (NominaIndividualDeAjuste, Replace or Delete) referencing the original CUNE. Form 350: yes, a corrective return. PILA: a correction return type N (correcciones) for the period, filed through the same operador as the original return, unless the Superintendencia Financiera has authorised that operador's wind-down; the operador settles the C records (correct values) minus the A records (original values), the C records must be equal to or greater than the A records in IBC and in days, and type N cannot be used for a correction that leads to a refund, which is requested from each administradora outside PILA (AT2 v30 §2.1.1.2.2 campo 8; Disposiciones comunes a la Planilla N; §2.1.2.3.9 campo 22). Return type M (mora) settles only periods before health period March 2014 with a total absence of payment; a correction that raises a value is made on type N, not on type M (AT2 v30 §2.1.1.2.2 campo 8, type M). |
| 42 | **═══ SPECIAL CASES ═══** |  |  |
| 43 | Health period one month ahead of the other subsystems | YES | T2R1-016 normally carries the month AFTER T2R1-015: health is paid one month in advance. Setting them equal is the classic first-run defect. |
| 44 | Employee on unpaid leave for the whole month | YES | Reported with the SLN flag, its date pair, and reduced day counts. The employment relationship subsists, so the return is still filed. |
| 45 | Employed old-age pensioner | YES | Contributor sub-type 01. The annex forces the pension rate in campo 46 to zero for sub-types 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 12. |
| 46 | Foreign employee with proven pension cover abroad | YES | Flagged in campo 7. No pension contribution is reported for the flagged foreign national (AT2 v30 §2.1.2.3.3); health, occupational risk and the levies remain. |
| 47 | Employee at more than one work centre with different risk classes | YES | The class attaches to the WORK CENTRE (Decree 1072 of 2015 art. 2.2.4.2.5.6). Where a person performs several occupations they contribute at the HIGHEST class; a mid-period move is reported through the VCT flag and its date pair. |
| 48 | Contributor type 40 (Beneficiary UPC Adicional) | PARTIAL | Reported as a detail record but EXCLUDED from the header contributor count in T2R1-019, and with its DIVIPOLA work-location fields blank. |
| 49 | Late payment | YES | A return paid after its deadline is filed on the ordinary return type E and the operador computes the interest on arrears (AT2 v30 §2.1.1.2.2 campo 8, type E). Return type M (mora) applies only to periods before health period March 2014 with a total absence of payment, and type N to a return already paid that is amended; T2R1-009 and T2R1-010 are blank on types E and M and carry the associated return number and date on type N (AT2 v30 §2.1.1.1 campos 9 and 10). |

THE SINGLE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL FLAG IN THE EMPLOYER RECORD. It declares that the employer is exonerated under ET art. 114-1 from the EMPLOYER health contribution of 8.5%, from the SENA levy of 2% and from the ICBF levy of 3%, for employees whose salary-constituting payments of the month are below 10 SMMLV (COP 17,509,050 in 2026) and whose health IBC is also below 10 SMMLV (DIAN Concepto 008380 de 2024; AT2 v30 campo 76). It does NOT touch pension, occupational risk or the family compensation fund 4%, none of which is ever exonerated. The per-employee side of the same test is Record Tipo 2 campo 76, and the DIAN side is Form 350 casilla 27 - configure the test once and consume it in all three places. Bidirectional set with the Record Tipo 2 exoneration fields: 'Contributor exonerated from payment' (T2R2-076), and the SENA and ICBF rate fields (T2R2-066 and T2R2-068) which must be ZERO wherever the ET art. 114-1 exoneration reaches the individual employee. | Y | -> Sheet 6: Exoneracion art. 114-1 | Not an amount - no rounding. | N | Flag | Monthly |  |  |

Bidirectional set with the fields this code gates: 'Work location department code' (T2R2-009) and 'Work location municipality code' (T2R2-010) are blank for type 40; 'Additional UPC value' (T2R2-056) is populated for type 40 and type 69; 'Principal contributor document type' (T2R2-074) only for type 40; 'Hours worked' (T2R2-096) is optional for types 1, 2, 18, 22, 30, 51 and 55; 'Termination date' (T2R2-081) is mandatory for type 75 (hire date T2R2-080 stays optional with ING); type 75 contributes to health, pension, occupational risk, CCF, SENA and ICBF on the monthly salary (never below 1 SMMLV), proportional to the days worked for health, pension and occupational risk, its health fund code (T2R2-033) must be MIN005 (ADRES) and the operador validates contributor and payer against the ADRES affiliates file for the period (AT2 v30 (24-07-2026) pp.132-133); and 'Pension fund of the member' (T2R2-031) may be blank only for a type not obliged to contribute to pension. Where marked, the engine populates 'Termination date' (T2R2-081) with the termination date (AT2 v30 (24-07-2026) campo 81 makes the date optional when RET is reported, except for contributor type 75, where it is mandatory; the engine's own interlock requires it). | Pos 138-138 | 1 | A(1) - alphanumeric, left-justified, SPACE-filled to the right |  | Payroll.Novedad_RET [Not an amount field -- a PILA novedad (change-event) code; no WTC code applies by design] | Marks the employee's exit from the systems settled in the return. AT2 v30 (MinSalud, Res. 2388/2016 Anexo Técnico 2, version 30, 24-07-2026) campo 16 (position 138, one character supplied by the contributor - 'suministrado por el aportante') admits blank, P, R, X, C or T. For a dependent employee the value is X (withdrawal from all the systems settled) in the period in which the termination date falls, and blank in every other period; P reports a withdrawal from the General Pension System only, and R and C apply to independent contributors. T is reported by the contracting party for independent contributors of type 59 in the planilla type Y and never applies to an employee. Pairs with the termination date in campo 81 (T2R2-081), optional under AT2 v30 when RET is reported and always populated by the engine, and drives the contributory days in campos 36 to 39, which run from the first day of the period to the termination date inclusive on the 30-day commercial month (a termination on the last calendar day of the month reports 30 days); the occupational-risk days follow the campo 38 rule (T2R2-038). Source: the termination date of the contract (Contract.End_Date), the same date as the final settlement's termination date and the electronic payroll FechaRetiro (NIE003). A termination processed after the return of its period was paid is reported for that period, not in the period in which the final settlement is paid, through a correction return (T2R1-008 = N) filed with the same operador that settled the original return, and only where the correction does not lower the contribution: the sum of IBC and the sum of days in the C records must each be equal to or greater than those in the A records, and return type N cannot be used for a correction that leads to a refund of amounts paid in excess (AT2 v30 §2.1.1.2.2 campo 8, type N, numerals 1 and 2; Disposiciones comunes a la Planilla N). A RET omitted from the original return of the same settlement period and filed on type N by the last business day of the month in which payment is due carries no interest on arrears (AT2 v30 type N numeral 2; section 16 'Manejo de planilla tipo N' item h). Where reporting the termination lowers the days or the IBC already paid, PILA is not the channel: the refund ('devolución o reintegro de aportes') is requested from each administradora that received the contributions. | Y | -> Sheet 6: Change events | Not an amount - no rounding. | N | Flag | Monthly |  |  |

| 150 | Contributor exonerated from payment | Cotizante exonerado de pago | File Type 2, Record Type 2 - Settlement | T2R2-076 | N | C | Marked where THIS EMPLOYEE, in THIS MONTH, earns less than 10 SMMLV (COP 17,509,050 in 2026) and the employer has declared itself exonerated in File Tipo 1 campo 33. Bidirectional set with A1-033 and with the SENA and ICBF rate and value fields T2R2-066 to T2R2-069 and the health rate T2R2-054, all of which must be consistent with it. HARD RULE printed at annex s.2.1.2.3.39: where 'Health contribution base' (T2R2-043) is at or above 10 SMMLV this field MUST be N - and likewise where a NATURAL-person employer employs two or more workers and the health base reaches 10 SMMLV. | Pos 506-506 | 1 | A(1) - alphanumeric, left-justified, SPACE-filled to the right | S | Payroll.Exoneration_Flag_Monthly [WTC: CO-FLAG-EXONERACION-114-1] | THE PER-EMPLOYEE, PER-MONTH SIDE of the ET art. 114-1 exoneration (introduced by Ley 1607 de 2012 and confirmed by Ley 1819 de 2016 art. 65). Values are S and N, not X. The employer-level flag in A1-033 declares eligibility; THIS field applies it to a specific employee in a specific month. TWO RULES APPLY TOGETHER. (1) The exoneration test counts the salary-constituting payments of the month only (CST art. 127): non-salary payments, vacation pay, social benefits and indemnities are left out (DIAN Concepto 008380 de 2024, confirmed by Concepto 007196 de 2025; Consejo de Estado, Seccion Cuarta, exp. 25302 de 2022 and 26984 de 2024; the 'totalidad de lo devengado' wording of Decreto 1828 de 2013 art. 7, compiled as DUR 1625 art. 1.5.1.4.1, was eliminated by Decreto 2201 de 2016): the employee qualifies where those salary payments of the month are below 10 SMMLV (COP 17,509,050 in 2026). (2) In addition, AT2 v30 campo 76 requires N whenever the health contribution base in campo 43 (T2R2-043) is at or above 10 SMMLV. The field is therefore S only where BOTH the salary payments of the month and the health IBC are below 10 SMMLV; where the salary is below 10 SMMLV but the health IBC reaches 10 SMMLV (Ley 1393 excess, vacation or incapacity IBC), report N and flag the case for review. The test is monthly, so an employee who crosses 10 SMMLV because of a bonus loses the exoneration for that month alone - the engine must evaluate it every period, never once a year. Where marked S, the employer's health 8.5%, SENA 2% and ICBF 3% fall away and the health rate in T2R2-054 becomes the EMPLOYEE rate alone (4%); pension, occupational risk and the CCF 4% remain payable in full. The engine sums only the salary-constituting payments of the month (non-salary payments, vacation pay, social benefits and indemnities excluded). | Y | -> Sheet 6: Exoneracion art. 114-1 | Not an amount - no rounding. | N | Flag | Monthly |  |  |

### Sheet: File Structure

FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS  
═══ SUBMISSION FORMAT ═══  

| Row | Channel | file_upload of two fixed-width flat files into the web portal of a LICENSED PRIVATE INFORMATION OPERATOR, or direct keying / call-centre entry on the same portal. The employer NEVER transacts directly with the government for social security. |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | Portal | The information operator chosen commercially by the employer. Operadores are licensed by the Ministry of Health and Social Protection. THIS IS NOT THE DIAN PORTAL: PILA never touches Muisca and Form 350 never touches an operador. |
| 5 | Source for the channel | Res. MSPS 2388 de 2016 Technical Annex 2, s.0 (File description) and s.2.1.1.2.1 (Return type); Decree 780 of 2016 art. 3.2.3.9 as substituted by Decree 1990 of 2016. |
| 6 | Modalities | 1 Electronica - the employer keys or uploads on the operador's web site. 2 Asistida - the operador's call centre keys it. Where Decree 780 art. 3.2.3.9 para. 2 exceptionally permits assisted payment, the field must still read ELECTRONICA and the operador reports those employers to the Ministry through SISPRO structure PUB019EXPE by the fifth business day of the following month. |
| 7 | Operator upload wrapper | The two files below are byte-exact against the official annex. Each operador's upload wrapper and any additional validations it layers on top are not publicly specified; they are published by each operador and held in the information-operator configuration for the operador the employer has chosen. |
| 8 | **═══ FILE FORMAT ═══** |  |
| 9 | File type | Two fixed-width flat text files, one record per line. |
| 10 | Numeric fields (tipo N) | Right-justified, ZERO-filled to the left. The annex states this expressly at s.0. |
| 11 | Alphanumeric fields (tipo A) | Left-justified, SPACE-filled to the right. |
| 12 | Record lengths | File Tipo 1 = 567 positions. File Tipo 2 Record Tipo 1 = 359 positions. File Tipo 2 Record Tipo 2 = 693 positions. All three equal the printed totals of AT2 v30 (24-07-2026). |
| 13 | Rounding | ROUND UP throughout. The contribution base is rounded up to the whole peso and each contribution value is rounded up to the NEXT MULTIPLE OF 100 (Decree 1990 of 2016 art. 1). This is a different convention from the electronic payroll (2 decimals, round-half-to-even) and from Form 350 (nearest 1,000). The same contribution therefore appears as different numbers in different artefacts. |
| 14 | Annual refresh obligation | The annex requires the employer to update ALL File Tipo 1 information with the operador from January 2018 onward, and to refresh it ANNUALLY. The operador must prompt for it. |
| 15 | **═══ RECORD STRUCTURE ═══** |  |
| 16 | File Tipo 1 | Datos generales del aportante. 34 campos, positions 1 to 567. ONE record per employer (or per branch where the form of presentation is S). |
| 17 | File Tipo 2, Record Tipo 1 | Encabezado. 22 campos, positions 1 to 359. ONE record. Identified by record type 01 in positions 1-2. |
| 18 | File Tipo 2, Record Tipo 2 | Detailed contribution settlement. 98 campos, positions 1 to 693. ONE record PER CONTRIBUTOR. Identified by record type 02 in positions 1-2, with a strictly sequential counter in positions 3-7 starting at 00001. |
| 19 | Records Tipo 3 to 12 | TOTALS RECORDS GENERATED BY THE OPERADOR, not by the employer. Type 3 total pension contributions; type 4 solidarity pension fund; type 5 health; type 6 occupational risk; type 7 family compensation funds; type 8 SENA; type 9 ICBF; type 10 ESAP; type 11 MEN; type 12 total payable for the period. They also carry the days-in-arrears count and the interest on arrears, which the operador computes from the payment date. The employer neither produces nor validates them, which is why they are OUT OF SCOPE for this Spec - but the engine must PARSE them from the settlement response to reconcile. |

| 49 | **═══ INBOUND - SETTLEMENT RESPONSE (INTEGRATION CO-IN-PILA-SETTLEMENT) ═══** |  |
| 50 | What comes back | The operador returns a settlement: the return number (matching T2R1-017), the payment date, the totals records (types 3 to 12) and any rejected contributor records. |
| 51 | What the engine must do | Reconcile the settled contributions against its own computation per subsystem; capture the return number and payment date as proof of compliance; and detect rejected contributor records so they can be re-filed on a correction return (type N). |
| 52 | Why no field-level spec here | Each operador's response layout is PROPRIETARY. There is no published national standard for it, so writing a field-level specification would be invention. The layout is published by the chosen information operator and held in the information-operator configuration. This is an upstream-owned interface: the operador owns the response layout; the engine owns the reconciliation, capture and rejection handling described above. |

### Sheet: Population Rules

POPULATION RULES - HOW TO FILL EACH FIELD FROM PAYROLL  

| Row | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | **═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES ═══** |  |  |  |
| 4 | The five contribution bases (T2R2-042 to T2R2-045 and T2R2-095) | Payroll engine | Compute and STORE five separate bases per employee per month. Three are the IBC for pension, health and occupational risk: total salary-constituting payments, plus the excess over the 40% non-salary clamp of Ley 1393 de 2010 art. 30, floored at 1 SMMLV (COP 1,750,905) and capped at 25 SMMLV (COP 43,772,625). Vacation paid in cash (during employment or on termination) is NOT a salary-constituting payment and is excluded from these three IBCs (Consejo de Estado, Sección Cuarta, exp. 26941 of 2024; unification ruling exp. 25185 of 2021, rule 1); for enjoyed vacation days, health and pension are contributed on the IBC of the month before the vacation starts (DUR 780 de 2016 art. 3.2.5.1; Consejo de Estado, Sección Cuarta, exp. 25958 of 2022). The fourth is the IBC CCF of campo 45: the monthly salary payroll of Ley 21 de 1982 art. 17, which INCLUDES paid rest days (70% of the integral salary, Ley 789 de 2002 art. 49), floored at 1 SMMLV and NOT capped at 25 SMMLV. The fifth is the PARAFISCAL base of campo 95, defined by the same Ley 21 de 1982 art. 17: it INCLUDES paid rest days and it is UNCAPPED. Never populate all five from one variable. | The four IBC values legitimately differ from one another once a change event enters - for example health may remain payable during an unpaid leave where pension does not. The header total in T2R1-020 is the sum of campo 45 (IBC CCF), NOT of campo 95 (AT2 v30 §2.1.1.1 campo 20); do not derive it from the parafiscal base. |
| 5 | The four day counts (T2R2-036 to T2R2-039) | Payroll engine | Maintain a contributory-day counter PER SUBSYSTEM on the 30-day commercial month. Start at 30 (or the proportion from a mid-month hire or to a mid-month leave), then apply the change events: SLN and lawful strike reduce all four; IGE and IRL follow the subsystem-specific rules; vacation and remunerated leave do not reduce the day counters (AT2 v30 §2.1.2.3.11 to §2.1.2.3.13), although no occupational-risk contribution is due for enjoyed vacation days (Decreto 1072 de 2015 art. 2.2.4.2.1.6 numeral 1.3; Consejo de Estado, Sección Cuarta, exp. 25958 of 2022). | February is 30 days and a 31-day month is 30 days. The counts must reconcile to the change event date pairs: a five-day SLN in a full month gives 25 contributory days and dates in T2R2-083 and T2R2-084 that span exactly five days. |
| 6 | Health period one month ahead (T2R1-016) | Engine (control) | Set the health payment period to the month AFTER the period in T2R1-015. Health is paid one month in advance; the other subsystems are paid in arrears. A March salary settlement carries period 2026-03 in T2R1-015 and 2026-04 in T2R1-016. | Setting the two equal is the single most common first-run defect. Note also the split of responsibility the annex records: T2R1-015 is CALCULATED BY THE OPERADOR, while T2R1-016 is SUPPLIED BY THE EMPLOYER. |
| 7 | Exoneration flags (A1-033 and T2R2-076) | Engine (control) | A1-033 is an EMPLOYER-LEVEL, standing declaration that the employer qualifies under ET art. 114-1. T2R2-076 is a PER-EMPLOYEE, PER-MONTH application of it, and may be S only where A1-033 is S. The employee test has two parts: (a) the salary-constituting payments of the month only (CST art. 127): non-salary payments, vacation pay, social benefits and indemnities are left out (DIAN Concepto 008380 de 2024, confirmed by Concepto 007196 de 2025; Consejo de Estado, Seccion Cuarta, exp. 25302 de 2022 and 26984 de 2024; the 'totalidad de lo devengado' wording of Decreto 1828 de 2013 art. 7, compiled as DUR 1625 art. 1.5.1.4.1, was eliminated by Decreto 2201 de 2016) must be BELOW 10 SMMLV = COP 17,509,050 in 2026 (ET art. 114-1); and (b) in addition, where the health base (T2R2-043) is at or above 10 SMMLV the field MUST be N (AT2 v30 campo 76). Where a NATURAL-person employer employs two or more workers and the base reaches 10 SMMLV it must also be N. Where T2R2-076 is S, set T2R2-054 to the EMPLOYEE rate alone (4.0000%), and set the SENA and ICBF rates and values (T2R2-066 to T2R2-069) to zero. | Because the test is MONTHLY, an employee who crosses 10 SMMLV in a bonus month loses the exoneration for that month alone and regains it the next. Evaluating it annually, or at hire, systematically under-contributes. The same test drives Form 350 casilla 27. |
| 8 | **═══ CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES ═══** |  |  |  |
| 9 | Header-to-detail consistency | Engine (validation) | Before submission assert: T2R1-004, 005, 006 and 007 equal File Tipo 1 campos 1, 2, 3 and 4 byte for byte; T2R1-011, 012 and 013 equal File Tipo 1 campos 10, 5 and 6; T2R1-021 equals File Tipo 1 campo 30; T2R1-019 equals the count of UNIQUE contributors in the detail EXCLUDING those with contributor type 40; and T2R1-020 equals the sum of T2R2-045 (IBC CCF, campo 45) across the detail. | The type-40 exclusion from the contributor count is easy to miss and produces a header-to-detail mismatch the operador rejects outright. |
| 10 | Pension rate forced to zero | Engine (validation) | Where the contributor sub-type (T2R2-006) is 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 or 12, the pension rate (T2R2-046) MUST be 0 and no pension contribution may be settled. | The electronic payroll equivalent is narrower - only SubTipoTrabajador 01 forces the rate to zero there. Map between the two lists; do not assume they agree. |
| 11 | Health rate may be zero only in two cases | Engine (validation) | The annex is explicit: T2R2-054 may be reported as zero ONLY where (a) SLN (T2R2-024) is X and the exoneration flag (T2R2-076) is S, or (b) SLN is C and the employer's legal nature is public. And where the health contribution (T2R2-055) is zero, the health days (T2R2-037), the health base (T2R2-043) and the health rate (T2R2-054) must ALL be zero - except for those same SLN-plus-exoneration contributors. | This is a four-field interlock. Implement it as one validation, not four independent ones. |
| 12 | Change event flag to date-pair interlock | Engine (validation) | Every marked change event flag must have its corresponding date field or pair populated, and every populated date field must have its flag marked: ING to 080, RET to 081, VSP to 082, SLN to 083 and 084, IGE to 085 and 086, LMA to 087 and 088, VAC-LR to 089 and 090, VCT to 091 and 092, IRL days to 093 and 094, TAE to 034, TAP to 032, AVP to 048 and 049. | Build the interlock as a table, not as a chain of conditionals - there are twelve pairs and a missed one produces a rejection at the operador rather than at Mercans. |
| 13 | Contribution calculation checks published in the annex | Engine (validation) | The annex prints the arithmetic the operador will apply: campo 55 = campo 43 x campo 54; campo 65 = campo 45 x campo 64; campo 67 = campo 95 x campo 66; campo 69 = campo 95 x campo 68; campo 71 = campo 95 x campo 70; campo 73 = campo 95 x campo 72. Note that the CCF uses the CCF base while SENA, ICBF, ESAP and MEN all use the PARAFISCAL base. | Reproduce these checks internally before submission. Each must then be rounded UP to the next multiple of 100. |
| 14 | **═══ AMOUNT FORMAT RULES ═══** |  |  |  |
| 15 | Rounding is UP, not to nearest | Engine (formatting) | Round the contribution base UP to the whole peso, and round EACH contribution value UP to the next multiple of 100 (Decree 1990 of 2016 art. 1). Worked illustration: occupational risk at class I on a base of 12,000,000 is 0.522% = 62,640, which becomes 62,700. | This is neither the electronic payroll convention (2 decimals, round-half-to-even) nor the Form 350 convention (nearest 1,000). Blending them produces reconciliation differences that look like errors but are not - the reconciliation must be run on the UNROUNDED values with a tolerance. |
| 16 | Numeric and alphanumeric justification | Engine (formatting) | Numeric fields are right-justified and ZERO-filled to the left; alphanumeric fields are left-justified and SPACE-filled to the right. The annex states this at s.0 and it applies without exception across all three records. | An empty numeric field is a run of zeros, not a run of spaces. This catches optional numeric fields such as A1-016 (Fax) and the unused parafiscal rate and value fields. |
| 17 | Rate fields: decimal with a point (e.g. 0.16000) | Engine (formatting) | The seven-position rate fields (T2R2-046, 054, 064, 066, 068, 070 and 072) are written as a decimal with a point, left-justified and zero-filled to the right (16% = 0.16000), as AT3 v15 p.63 prints for the same ministry and length ('por ejemplo 2.0% seria 0.02000') and as the AT2 v30 output layout states ('Tarifa. En decimales', p.210). The nine-position occupational-risk rate (T2R2-061) follows the same rule, zero-filled to nine positions (0.522% = 0.0052200), because the AT2 v30 output layout copies it to the occupational-risk administrators as 'Tarifa. En decimales' (p.210). Confirm with the information operator during set-up. | This is the one presentation detail of the layout that the annex leaves under-specified. |
| 18 | **═══ PAYROLL-SPECIFIC POPULATION RULES ═══** |  |  |  |
| 19 | The 40% non-salary clamp | Payroll engine | Total remuneration for the period = salary payments + payments agreed as non-salary under an express CST art. 128 pact + paid leave; indemnities, unpaid leave, incapacities and social benefits are left out (UGPP, ABC Empleadores 2025). Where the pacted non-salary payments exceed 40% of total remuneration, add the EXCESS back into the three contribution bases for pension, health and occupational risk (Ley 1393 de 2010 art. 30; Consejo de Estado, Sección Cuarta, sentencia de unificación exp. 25185 of 9 December 2021, rule 3); the CCF and parafiscal bases of Ley 21 de 1982 art. 17 do not take it. Payments that are non-salary by nature or by law (transport allowance, occasional per diem, means and tools to do the job, mere liberality) stay out of both sides of the test (Consejo de Estado, Sección Cuarta, sentencia de unificación exp. 25185 of 9 December 2021, rule 3; UGPP, ABC Empleadores 2025). Store the added-back amount as its own quantity: it is IN the contribution base but OUT of the statutory-benefit base for cesantias, prima and the severance indemnity. | The clamp is computed on the period's totals, so a single large non-salary bonus can push an otherwise compliant employee over the line for one month. It also interacts with the exoneration test, because the added-back amount raises the health base toward the 10-SMMLV threshold. |
| 20 | All-inclusive salary at 70% | Payroll engine | Where the employee is on all-inclusive salary (CST art. 132 num. 2, minimum 13 SMMLV = COP 22,761,765 in 2026), mark T2R2-041 and set the four IBC fields to 70% of the integral salary. The remaining 30% is the statutory prestacional factor and is not a contribution base. Where pacted non-salary payments exceed 40% of total remuneration, the excess is added to the pension, health and occupational-risk IBC without the 70% reduction: IBC = 70% of the integral salary + excess (Ley 100 de 1993 art. 18; Consejo de Estado SU 25185 de 2021, rule 3; exp. 25907 de 2022); the CCF and parafiscal bases stay at 70% of the integral salary. | Note the interaction with the ceiling: 70% of a large integral salary can still exceed 25 SMMLV, in which case the ceiling applies to the 70% figure, not to the full salary - for the pension, health and occupational-risk IBC only; the CCF base (T2R2-045) and the parafiscal base (T2R2-095) take the 70% figure without a ceiling. |
| 21 | Work centre and risk class | Employee master data | Carry the work centre on the employee record and derive the risk class from it, not from the employer. Where an employee performs several occupations, contribute at the HIGHEST class (Decree 1072 of 2015 art. 2.2.4.2.5.6). Where the employee moves work centre mid-period, mark VCT (T2R2-029) and populate T2R2-091 and T2R2-092. | A mid-period move can change the ARL rate; the annex does not prescribe a split of the period between the two work centres. |
| 22 | Foreign employee electing out of pension | Employee master data | Mark T2R2-007 only for a foreign national for whom the employer has configured, as an option per employee and with the citation Ley 100 de 1993 art. 15 num. 2 (as modified by Ley 797 de 2003 art. 3), that pension affiliation does not apply (foreigners who remain in the country under an employment contract and are not covered by a pension regime of their country of origin or of any other country are voluntary affiliates). Health, occupational risk and the parafiscal levies remain fully payable. The flag narrows the valid document types to CE, PA, CD, SC, PE and PT. | THIS IS NOT A TAX FIELD. It says nothing about tax residence: the same employee may be withheld at the flat 20% of ET art. 408 on sheet 2 of Form 350 while contributing to Colombian health and occupational risk on ordinary terms. |
| 23 | Incapacity and leave advanced by the employer | Payroll engine | Colombian employers universally ADVANCE the EPS and ARL benefits through payroll and recover from the institution. Model the benefit as PAID to the employee and RECEIVABLE from the institution, but do NOT report it in the PILA: fields T2R2-057 to T2R2-060 (IGE and LMA authorisation numbers and values) are always blank / zero under AT2 v30, so the IGE and LMA amounts and authorisation numbers are kept in payroll for the reimbursement claim only. | Without the authorisation number the institution will not reimburse. The employer's first-two-days rate for general illness (Mercans default 66.67%) and the one-minimum-wage floor on incapacity pay are configurable client elections maintained in the payroll configuration; neither is reported in PILA. |
| 24 | **═══ CROSS-FIELD VALIDATIONS ═══** |  |  |  |
| 25 | A1-009 drives A1-004, A1-018, A1-020, A1-021 and A1-023 | Engine (validation) | Where the employer person type is J, the verification digit and the legal representative's identification number, document type, first surname and first name are all mandatory. Where it is N, the verification digit must be ZERO and the legal-representative block is optional. | Note the asymmetry: A1-019 (the representative's own verification digit) is ALWAYS zero whatever the person type, because the annex says so expressly. |
| 26 | A1-010 drives A1-005 and A1-006 | Engine (validation) | Where the form of presentation is U, the branch code and name must be BLANK. Where it is S, both must be populated - and where the branch has no name, the annex directs that the CODE be repeated in the name field. | The same interlock repeats at T2R1-011, T2R1-012 and T2R1-013. |
| 27 | T2R1-008 drives T2R1-009 and T2R1-010 | Engine (validation) | Where the return type is E, A, I, M, S, Y, H, T, X, K, Q or B, both associated-return fields must be blank (AT2 v30 (24-07-2026) p.27 campo 9). Where it is N or F they carry the period return; where it is U, the judicial deposit title; where it is J or O, the return of the original payment. | The annex adds that where the operador cannot find the initial return for that contributor and period, it must NOT permit the correction return at all. |
| 28 | A1-007 = D drives A1-031, A1-032 and A1-034 | Engine (validation) | A Ley 1429 de 2010 beneficiary must carry the commercial-registry date and the registered department, and the registry date must fall between 29 December 2010 and 31 December 2014. | The window is closed and historical: an employer registered after 2014 cannot be class D, whatever its size. |
| 29 | T2R2-008 drives T2R2-009, T2R2-010 and T2R2-097 | Engine (validation) | Where 'Colombiano en el exterior' is marked, the DIVIPOLA work-location department and municipality must be BLANK and the foreign filing date becomes relevant. The flag is available only for document types CC and TI. | Contributor type 40 also blanks the two DIVIPOLA fields, for a different reason. |
| 30 | Cross-report reconciliation | Engine (reconciliation) | After settlement assert: T2R2-055 (employee portion) reconciles to electronic payroll NIE163; the employee 4% within T2R2-047 reconciles to NIE166; T2R2-051 and T2R2-052 reconcile to NIE168 and NIE170. Reconcile on the UNROUNDED values with a tolerance of 100 pesos per contribution, because PILA rounds up to the next 100 and the XML does not. | The employer-borne amounts - pension 12%, health 8.5%, occupational risk, CCF, SENA, ICBF - have NO electronic payroll counterpart at all and cannot be reconciled to it. They reconcile only to the employer-cost ledger. |

The three records below were GENERATED PROGRAMMATICALLY by placing each  
value at the position published in the official Technical Annex 2 (Resolution  
MSPS 2388 de 2016, AT2 version 30, 24-07-2026) and applying the annex's own  
justification rules - numeric fields right-justified and zero-filled,  
alphanumeric fields left-justified and space-filled.  
The record lengths are therefore EXACT, not approximate:  
Archivo Tipo 1 567 characters (annex total: 567)  
Archivo Tipo 2, Registro Tipo 1 359 characters (annex total: 359)  
Archivo Tipo 2, Registro Tipo 2 693 characters (annex total: 693)  
This is NOT an official MSPS sample file - none is published - but the  
LAYOUT is the official layout, byte for byte. What each operador de  
information wraps around these two files, and what additional validations it  
applies, is operador-specific and is held in the information-operator configuration.  
Administradora codes (AFP001, EPS001, CCF001, ARL001) are illustrative valueS. The  
real six-position codes are the Ministry catalogue codes distributed by the chosen operador.  
Values are the worked example on the Example Analysis sheet: MERCANS  
COLOMBIA S.A.S., NIT 900123456-8, one contributor on COP 12,000,000 for

These records also carry the days-in-arrears count and the interest on  
arrears, which the operador computes from the payment date. The employer  
neither produces nor validates them - but the ENGINE MUST PARSE THEM from  
the settlement response in order to reconcile, capture the return number  
and payment date, and detect rejected contributor records.
